_meta.purpose: Coaching note per syllabus topic: plain-language idea, must-know rules/formulas, and the exam angle. Also used to ground the AI tutor.

CPA|FAR|Conceptual framework.idea: The rulebook behind the rulebook. It says what makes financial information useful and what assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses are.
key: Fundamental qualities: relevance (predictive, confirmatory, materiality) and faithful representation (complete, neutral, free from error).
Enhancing qualities: comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability.
Cost constraint: benefits of information should justify its cost.
Asset = present right to an economic benefit. Liability = present obligation to transfer one.
CPA|FAR|Conceptual framework.tip: Questions are mostly 'which characteristic is this?' Memorise the two lists.

CPA|FAR|Financial statements & cash flow.idea: Profit is an opinion, cash is a fact. The cash flow statement explains why cash changed.
key: Indirect method: net income ± non-cash items ± working-capital changes.
US GAAP: interest paid/received and dividends received are operating; dividends paid are financing.
Significant non-cash activities are disclosed separately.
CPA|FAR|Financial statements & cash flow.tip: Watch the sign of working-capital changes. That's where most marks are lost.

CPA|FAR|Revenue recognition.idea: Count revenue when you hand over what you promised, at the price the customer agreed.
key: 5 steps: contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate, recognise.
Allocate by relative standalone selling price.
Variable consideration is constrained (only if a significant reversal is not probable).
Over time if: simultaneous receipt/consumption, customer-controlled asset, or no alternative use + right to payment.
CPA|FAR|Revenue recognition.tip: Bundles with discounts = allocation questions. Practise the ratio maths.

CPA|FAR|Receivables.idea: Money customers owe you, reduced by what you realistically expect to lose.
key: CECL: lifetime expected credit losses from day one.
Allowance method; expense = required ending allowance − existing balance (adjust for the debit/credit side).
Write-offs hit the allowance, not expense.
Factoring with recourse may be a borrowing, not a sale.
CPA|FAR|Receivables.tip: Draw the allowance T-account. Most questions are a missing figure in it.

CPA|FAR|Inventory.idea: Goods held for sale, carried at what they cost unless you'd get less for them.
key: Rising prices: FIFO gives the highest inventory and profit; LIFO gives the highest COGS.
FIFO/average: lower of cost and NRV. LIFO/retail: lower of cost or market.
Consignment goods belong to the consignor.
formula: NRV = selling price − costs to complete and sell
CPA|FAR|Inventory.tip: Cut-off and ownership (FOB shipping point vs destination) are frequent traps.

CPA|FAR|PP&E and depreciation.idea: Long-life assets are recorded at cost, then that cost is spread over their useful life.
key: Capitalise all costs to get the asset ready for use (freight, installation, testing).
Straight-line, declining balance (ignore salvage in the rate), units of production.
Changes in life/method are changes in estimate, so prospective.
Interest during construction is capitalised for qualifying assets.
CPA|FAR|PP&E and depreciation.tip: Stop depreciating once book value reaches salvage.

CPA|FAR|Impairment & intangibles.idea: If an asset will never earn back its book value, write it down.
key: Held & used: test with undiscounted cash flows; measure the loss with fair value; no reversal.
Goodwill (public entities): not amortised; annual impairment test; loss = carrying amount − fair value of the reporting unit (capped at goodwill).
R&D: expensed (US GAAP); software for sale capitalised after technological feasibility.
Indefinite-life intangibles: not amortised, tested annually.
CPA|FAR|Impairment & intangibles.tip: Two numbers for impairment: one to TEST, one to MEASURE. Never mix them.

CPA|FAR|Investments.idea: How you account for owning another company's shares or bonds depends on how much influence you have.
key: Under 20% equity: fair value through net income.
20–50% (significant influence): equity method (share of income adds, dividends subtract).
CPA|FAR|Investments.tip: Equity method dividends are a return OF investment, never income.

CPA|FAR|Leases.idea: A long rental is really borrowing to buy, so it goes on the balance sheet.
key: Lessee recognises an ROU asset + lease liability (except leases of 12 months or less, if elected).
Finance lease if any of: ownership transfer, purchase option reasonably certain, major part of life, PV ≈ all of fair value, specialised asset.
CPA|FAR|Leases.tip: IFRS 16 / Ind AS 116 have one lessee model. Know the difference for exam traps.

CPA|FAR|Bonds and liabilities.idea: Borrowing via bonds. The price adjusts so investors earn the market rate.
key: Coupon < market rate: discount. Coupon > market rate: premium.
Effective interest: expense = carrying amount × market rate.
Issue costs reduce the carrying amount.
Early extinguishment gain/loss = carrying amount − price paid.
CPA|FAR|Bonds and liabilities.tip: Build the amortisation table for 2 periods. It answers most questions.

CPA|FAR|Contingencies.idea: Possible future losses from past events, like lawsuits.
key: Probable + estimable: accrue (US GAAP uses the minimum of a range if no best estimate).
Gain contingencies: never recognised until realised.
CPA|FAR|Contingencies.tip: IFRS 'probable' = more likely than not, and the midpoint is used for ranges.

CPA|FAR|Income taxes.idea: Book profit and taxable profit differ. Deferred taxes bridge the timing gaps.
key: Temporary differences create DTAs/DTLs; permanent ones never do (e.g., municipal interest, fines).
Use the enacted rate for the reversal years.
Valuation allowance if a DTA is more likely than not to be unrealisable.
CPA|FAR|Income taxes.tip: Ask 'more or less tax in future?' to pick DTL vs DTA.

CPA|FAR|Equity & EPS.idea: The owners' share, and how much profit each ordinary share earned.
key: Basic EPS = (NI − preferred dividends) / weighted average shares.
Stock dividends and splits are retroactive. Issues and buybacks are time-weighted.
Diluted EPS: if-converted (convertibles), treasury stock method (options).
Small stock dividend at fair value; large one at par.
CPA|FAR|Equity & EPS.tip: Antidilutive securities are excluded from diluted EPS.

CPA|FAR|Business combinations.idea: Buying control of another company. You record its assets at fair value, and any extra paid becomes goodwill.
key: Acquisition method; acquisition costs are expensed.
Goodwill = consideration + NCI fair value − fair value of net identifiable assets.
Eliminate intercompany balances and profits on consolidation.
CPA|FAR|Business combinations.tip: Intercompany inventory profit elimination is a favourite simulation.

CPA|FAR|Accounting changes & errors.idea: Change a rule → restate the past. Change a guess → go forward. Fix a mistake → restate.
key: Error correction: prior-period adjustment to opening retained earnings.

CPA|FAR|Governmental accounting.idea: Governments track spendable money in funds AND the full economic picture government-wide.
key: Governmental funds: modified accrual, current financial resources.
Proprietary and fiduciary funds and government-wide statements: full accrual.
Budgetary entries: estimated revenues, appropriations, encumbrances.
Reconciliation from fund to government-wide statements.
CPA|FAR|Governmental accounting.tip: Know which fund type each activity goes in (General, Special Revenue, Capital Projects, Debt Service, Permanent, Enterprise, Internal Service, Trust).

CPA|FAR|Not-for-profit accounting.idea: Charities report what they hold and whether donors restricted it.
key: Net assets: with / without donor restrictions.
Unconditional promises are recognised when made. Conditional ones when the barrier is met.
Expenses by nature AND function (program vs support).
Contributed services recognised only if they create an asset or need specialised skills.
CPA|FAR|Not-for-profit accounting.tip: Restriction ≠ condition. Restricted gifts are revenue now.

CPA|AUD|Ethics and independence.idea: Auditors must be independent in fact and in appearance, or their opinion is worthless.
key: Direct financial interest: always impairs independence.
Indirect interest: impairs only if material.
Non-attest services need management to take responsibility.

CPA|AUD|Engagement acceptance & planning.idea: Decide whether to take the client, agree terms, then plan the audit around risk.
key: Communicate with the predecessor auditor (with client permission) before accepting.
Analytics are required in planning and final review.
CPA|AUD|Engagement acceptance & planning.tip: Know the order: accept → engagement letter → understand the entity → assess risk → respond.

CPA|AUD|Audit risk.idea: The risk the auditor gives a clean opinion on wrong accounts.
key: RMM (IR × CR) is the client's; DR is the auditor's lever.
Higher RMM means lower DR, which means more, better and later substantive testing.
CPA|AUD|Audit risk.tip: Inverse relationship between RMM and DR is tested every exam.

CPA|AUD|Internal control.idea: The company's own system for preventing and catching mistakes and fraud.
key: COSO: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information & communication, monitoring.
Tests of controls only if planning to rely on them.
Significant deficiency vs material weakness communication.
CPA|AUD|Internal control.tip: Match each control to the risk it prevents. Simulations love this.

CPA|AUD|Audit evidence.idea: Sufficient, appropriate proof for each assertion.
key: Assertions: existence/occurrence, completeness, rights, valuation, presentation, cut-off, accuracy.
Vouch (records→docs) for existence; trace (docs→records) for completeness.
External, auditor-obtained, documentary evidence is strongest.
Subsequent events: recognised (existing condition) vs non-recognised.
CPA|AUD|Audit evidence.tip: Direction of testing determines the assertion.

CPA|AUD|Audit sampling.idea: Test a sample to conclude about the whole population.
key: Incorrect acceptance and assessing control risk too low = effectiveness risks.
Sample size rises with risk and expected error, and falls with tolerable misstatement.
MUS (PPS) favours large items and suits overstatement.
Projected misstatement + allowance for sampling risk vs tolerable.
CPA|AUD|Audit sampling.tip: Draw arrows: which inputs push sample size up or down.

CPA|AUD|Audit reports.idea: The auditor's one-page verdict on the accounts.
key: Scope limitation: material → qualified; pervasive → disclaimer.

CPA|AUD|Review & compilation engagements.idea: Lighter services than an audit for smaller clients.
key: Review: limited assurance; inquiry + analytics; independence required.
Compilation: no assurance; independence impairment must be disclosed.
CPA|AUD|Review & compilation engagements.tip: Which procedures are NOT done in a review: confirmations, observation, tests of controls.

CPA|REG|Professional responsibilities.idea: Rules for tax practitioners dealing with the IRS and clients.
key: Circular 230: due diligence, advise of errors, no unreasonable positions.
Statute of limitations: 3 years; 6 years for >25% omission; unlimited for fraud.
CPA|REG|Professional responsibilities.tip: Your duty is to ADVISE the client, not to report them.

CPA|REG|Business law.idea: Contracts, agency, secured transactions, bankruptcy and business structures.
key: Contract: offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, legality.
Statute of Frauds writings (land, over 1 year, goods $500+).
CPA|REG|Business law.tip: Priority rules in Article 9 are a classic multi-step question.

CPA|REG|Property basis.idea: Basis is your tax 'price tag' for a property. Gain = amount realised − basis.
key: Gift: donor's basis (dual-basis rule for losses).
CPA|REG|Property basis.tip: Gift vs inheritance is the #1 trap.

CPA|REG|Property transactions.idea: Selling or swapping property: when gains are taxed and at what rate.
key: §1031 like-kind (real property only): recognise the lesser of boot or gain.
§1231 net gain → LTCG; net loss → ordinary; 5-year look-back.
CPA|REG|Property transactions.tip: Compute realised, then recognised, then new basis, in that order.

CPA|REG|Individual taxation.idea: How a person's taxable income and tax are built up.
key: Gross income → adjustments (for AGI) → AGI → standard or itemised deduction → taxable income.
Credits reduce tax dollar-for-dollar; deductions reduce income.
CPA|REG|Individual taxation.tip: Year-specific amounts change. Learn the STRUCTURE first, then the current-year figures from your review course.

CPA|REG|Entity taxation.idea: How C corps, S corps and partnerships are taxed.
key: §351 formation: no gain if 80% control; carryover basis.
Partnership basis: + contributions, income, liabilities; − distributions, losses.
S corp: ≤100 shareholders, one class of stock, no nonresident aliens.
CPA|REG|Entity taxation.tip: Outside basis questions are pure arithmetic. Practise the generator.

CPA|BAR|Cost-volume-profit.idea: How many units you must sell to cover costs and make a target profit.
key: Break-even units = fixed costs / CM per unit.
Margin of safety = actual sales − break-even sales.
CPA|BAR|Cost-volume-profit.tip: With a tax rate, gross up the after-tax target: profit / (1 − t).

CPA|BAR|Financial statement analysis.idea: Ratios turn statements into answers: is the company liquid, efficient, profitable, safe?
CPA|BAR|Financial statement analysis.tip: Know which ratios use averages and which use COGS vs sales.

CPA|BAR|Cost & variance analysis.idea: Compare what things SHOULD have cost with what they DID cost, and explain why.
key: Price/rate variance: (actual − standard price) × actual quantity.
Efficiency/usage variance: (actual − standard quantity) × standard price.
Absorption vs variable costing income difference = Δinventory × fixed overhead/unit.

CPA|BAR|Decision making.idea: Only future costs that DIFFER between options matter.
key: Sunk and unavoidable costs are irrelevant.
Make or buy, special orders, keep or drop, sell or process further.
Constrained resources: maximise CM per scarce unit.
CPA|BAR|Decision making.tip: A special order at below full cost can still be profitable. Look at variable cost and capacity.

CPA|BAR|Advanced technical accounting.idea: Complex areas: derivatives and hedging, leases for lessors, and more.
key: Fair value hedge: both sides through earnings.
Cash flow hedge: OCI, then reclassified.
CPA|BAR|Advanced technical accounting.tip: Match the hedge type to the risk: fixed-rate asset → fair value hedge; forecast purchase → cash flow hedge.

CPA|ISC|SOC engagements.idea: Reports on a service provider's controls, so its customers' auditors can rely on them.
key: SOC 1: controls over the user's financial reporting.
SOC 2: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy (restricted use).
Type 1 = design at a point in time; Type 2 = design + operating effectiveness over a period.
CUECs and carve-out vs inclusive methods.
CPA|ISC|SOC engagements.tip: Auditor relying on controls → SOC 1 Type 2.

CPA|ISC|IT general controls.idea: Controls over the whole IT environment that keep application controls trustworthy.
key: Application controls: input, processing, output checks.
CPA|ISC|IT general controls.tip: A weak ITGC undermines reliance on automated controls.

CPA|ISC|Data security.idea: Protect data's confidentiality, integrity and availability.
CPA|ISC|Data security.tip: Key direction questions: write out who holds which key.

CPA|ISC|Data management & continuity.idea: Keep data accurate, governed and recoverable.
key: RPO = acceptable data loss; RTO = acceptable downtime.
CPA|ISC|Data management & continuity.tip: RPO drives backup frequency. RTO drives recovery site choice.

CPA|TCP|Individual planning.idea: Arrange personal finances to legally reduce tax.
key: Retirement accounts: traditional (pre-tax) vs Roth (after-tax, tax-free growth).
CPA|TCP|Individual planning.tip: Compare tax now vs tax later with expected rates.

CPA|TCP|Entity planning.idea: Choose and use the right business structure for tax.
key: C corp double tax vs flow-through.
CPA|TCP|Entity planning.tip: Questions ask for the BEST entity for given facts. List the pros and cons.

CPA|TCP|Gift and estate.idea: Taxes on transferring wealth during life (gift) or at death (estate).
key: Annual exclusion per donee; gift splitting.
Gross estate includes life insurance with incidents of ownership.
CPA|TCP|Gift and estate.tip: Exclusion amounts are indexed. Check the current year's figures.

CPA|TCP|Property planning.idea: Time and structure property sales to manage tax.
CPA|TCP|Property planning.tip: Recapture is recognised in the year of sale even under the installment method.

FRM|P1-FRM|Risk governance.idea: Who decides how much risk to take, and who checks it.
key: Board approves risk appetite; management executes.
Three lines: business, risk/compliance, internal audit.
FRM|P1-FRM|Risk governance.tip: Questions test roles. Ask 'who owns, who oversees, who assures?'

FRM|P1-FRM|CAPM.idea: Expected return = safe return + reward for market risk (beta).
FRM|P1-FRM|CAPM.tip: Watch for questions that give Rm and ask you to remember to subtract Rf.

FRM|P1-FRM|Risk-adjusted performance.idea: Was the return worth the risk?
key: Information ratio = active return / tracking error.
FRM|P1-FRM|Risk-adjusted performance.tip: Pick the right risk measure for the investor's situation (diversified → Treynor).

FRM|P1-FRM|Case studies & ethics.idea: Famous disasters teach what goes wrong in risk management.
key: Barings: no segregation of trading and settlement.
Metallgesellschaft: funding liquidity of a hedge.
London Whale: model changes and governance.
FRM|P1-FRM|Case studies & ethics.tip: Match each case to its main failure.

FRM|P1-QA|Probability.idea: Measuring how likely things are, and updating beliefs with new information.
key: Expected value and variance of discrete variables.
FRM|P1-QA|Probability.tip: Write a 2×2 table of counts (e.g., 10,000 people). It makes Bayes trivial.

key: Normal, lognormal, t, chi-square, F, Poisson, binomial.
Hypothesis tests, Type I/II errors, p-values.
FRM|P1-QA|Statistics & distributions.tip: Know which distribution suits which test (t for means, χ² for variance, F for comparing variances).

FRM|P1-QA|Portfolio statistics.idea: Risk of a mix of assets depends on how they move together.
key: Diversification benefit rises as ρ falls.
FRM|P1-QA|Portfolio statistics.tip: Always square-root the variance at the end.

FRM|P1-QA|Regression.idea: Fit a line to explain one variable with others.
key: Problems: heteroskedasticity (robust SE), multicollinearity, omitted variables (bias).
FRM|P1-QA|Regression.tip: Know the cause and effect of each OLS assumption failure.

FRM|P1-QA|Time series & simulation.idea: Model data that evolves over time, and simulate outcomes.
key: Monte Carlo; variance reduction (antithetic, control variates).
FRM|P1-QA|Time series & simulation.tip: Seasonality and trend removal come before modelling.

FRM|P1-FMP|Forwards and futures.idea: Agreements to trade later at a price fixed today.
key: Futures: daily settlement, margin calls (restore to initial).
Hedge ratio h* = ρσS/σF; contracts = β·P/(F·m).
FRM|P1-FMP|Forwards and futures.tip: Margin calls restore to INITIAL margin.

FRM|P1-FMP|Swaps.idea: Exchange one stream of cash flows for another.
key: Value = difference of two bonds, or a portfolio of FRAs.
FRM|P1-FMP|Swaps.tip: Value a swap as long one bond, short the other.

FRM|P1-FMP|Options.idea: The right, not the obligation, to buy (call) or sell (put).
key: Put-call parity: C + PV(K) = P + S.
Bounds; American calls on non-dividend stocks are never exercised early.
FRM|P1-FMP|Options.tip: Draw the payoff diagram for any strategy question.

FRM|P1-FMP|Bonds.idea: Loans that trade. Price is the present value of cash flows.
key: Coupon vs yield gives par, premium or discount.
Day counts, accrued interest, clean vs dirty price.
FRM|P1-FMP|Bonds.tip: Dirty price = clean price + accrued interest.

FRM|P1-FMP|Interest & FX rates.idea: Rates for different maturities and currencies are linked by no-arbitrage.
key: Covered interest parity: F = S(1 + r_d)/(1 + r_f).
FRM|P1-FMP|Interest & FX rates.tip: Check which currency is the price currency in FX quotes.

FRM|P1-FMP|Clearing & securitised produc.idea: CCPs reduce counterparty risk; MBS pass mortgage cash flows to investors.

FRM|P1-VRM|Value at Risk.idea: A loss level you won't exceed with a given confidence over a horizon.
key: VaR is not subadditive and ignores tail severity.

FRM|P1-VRM|Expected shortfall.idea: The average loss on the days that are worse than VaR.
key: ES ≥ VaR at the same confidence.
FRM|P1-VRM|Expected shortfall.tip: With discrete scenarios, average the tail losses.

FRM|P1-VRM|Duration and convexity.idea: How sensitive a bond's price is to yield changes.
key: Positive convexity always helps the bondholder.

FRM|P1-VRM|Option valuation & Greeks.idea: Pricing options and measuring their sensitivities.
key: Delta, gamma (highest ATM near expiry), vega, theta, rho.
FRM|P1-VRM|Option valuation & Greeks.tip: Short options = negative gamma = hedges need constant rebalancing.

FRM|P1-VRM|Credit ratings & stress testi.idea: Ratings summarise credit quality; stress tests ask 'what if?'
key: Scenario vs sensitivity vs reverse stress tests.
FRM|P1-VRM|Credit ratings & stress testi.tip: Reverse stress test = start from failure and work back.

FRM|P2-MR|Backtesting.idea: Check whether VaR predictions matched reality.
key: Basel zones: green 0–4, yellow 5–9, red 10+ (250 days, 99%).
Liquidity-adjusted VaR = VaR + ½ spread × value.
FRM|P2-MR|Backtesting.tip: Type I = rejecting a good model; Type II = accepting a bad one.

key: Stricter boundary between banking and trading books.
FRM|P2-MR|FRTB.tip: Know WHY ES replaced VaR: tail risk and subadditivity.

FRM|P2-MR|Volatility models.idea: Volatility changes over time, and these models track it.
key: GARCH(1,1): adds a long-run variance term; V_L = ω/(1 − α − β).
FRM|P2-MR|Volatility models.tip: Work with variances, then take the square root.

FRM|P2-MR|Term structure & volatility sm.idea: Models of how rates evolve and why implied volatility varies by strike.
FRM|P2-MR|Term structure & volatility sm.tip: Equity puts carry a crash premium, which creates the skew.

FRM|P2-CR|Expected loss.idea: Average credit loss to price in; capital covers the surprise beyond it.
key: UL and credit VaR = quantile − EL.

FRM|P2-CR|Counterparty risk.idea: Risk the other side of a derivative defaults while owing you.
FRM|P2-CR|Counterparty risk.tip: Netting only applies under an enforceable agreement.

FRM|P2-CR|Credit derivatives & securitis.idea: Transfer credit risk via CDS and tranches.
FRM|P2-CR|Credit derivatives & securitis.tip: Higher correlation hurts senior tranches and helps equity.

key: Merton: equity = call on assets; distance to default.
FRM|P2-CR|Credit risk models.tip: Higher asset volatility → higher equity value, lower debt value.

FRM|P2-OR|Basel operational risk capital.idea: Capital for losses from failed processes, people, systems or external events.
FRM|P2-OR|Basel operational risk capital.tip: AMA is gone. Know the new components.

FRM|P2-OR|Operational risk management.idea: Identify, measure and control operational losses.

FRM|P2-OR|Model risk & resilience.idea: Models can be wrong; businesses must withstand disruptions.
key: SR 11-7: development, validation, governance, effective challenge.
Operational resilience: important services, impact tolerances.

FRM|P2-LT|LCR and NSFR.idea: Basel liquidity ratios: survive 30 days of stress (LCR), fund stably for a year (NSFR).
key: LCR = HQLA / net outflows (30 days) ≥ 100%; inflows capped at 75%.
HQLA levels 1, 2A, 2B with haircuts and caps.
FRM|P2-LT|LCR and NSFR.tip: Apply the inflow cap before dividing.

FRM|P2-LT|Asset-liability management.idea: Manage mismatches between assets and liabilities.
FRM|P2-LT|Asset-liability management.tip: Negative gap: hurt by rising rates.

FRM|P2-RMIM|Portfolio risk.tip: Hedging positions can have negative component VaR.

FRM|P2-RMIM|Performance & hedge funds.idea: Measure manager skill and understand alternatives.
FRM|P2-RMIM|Performance & hedge funds.tip: Allocation uses the benchmark sector return minus the benchmark total.

FRM|P2-CI|Current issues (annual reading.idea: Topical readings chosen by GARP each year.
key: Read only the current year's list.
Focus on conclusions and risk implications.
FRM|P2-CI|Current issues (annual reading.tip: Typically conceptual. Easy marks if read.
